svg.title: Figure 11 — Production-Grade Parallel Stack versus Autonomous Frontier Closure
svg.desc: Two nested closure tests: seven production-grade gates and two additional continuity gates required for autonomous frontier closure.
svg.text: China frontier assessment requires two separate closure tests
Production deployment can become economically meaningful before full multi-generation autonomy is established.
Question: can the system work commercially at verifiable scale?
Includes all seven production-grade gates, plus:
equipment / software / materials / spares / service / process upgrades
HBM / packaging / LPS / power / long-duration capital
Question: can the stack keep scaling when critical external inputs are constrained?
Current evidence · Aug 28, 2026: partial production deployment is real; the seven Production-Grade Gates are not all publicly closed.
Source: Report framework and current-state synthesis; Chapters 17 and 32.
Boundary: production-grade substitution ≠ full technological autonomy; import dependence also does not prove that no production-grade parallel stack exists.
